normalization_policy: normalized claim plus artifact and evidence target; no voting

findings.claim: The final acceptance projection has an unclosed cross-artifact revocation race: it re-reads P16 authority and revocation state before a version-guarded execution-ledger write, but defines no atomic guard over the authority source, so a revocation committed after that read and before the write can still persist ACCEPTED despite the categorical no-write claim.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Drift, revocation or unavailable observation writes no final bytes
findings.impact: A revoked HUMAN decision can be projected as accepted and become dependency-satisfying during the undisclosed acceptance check-to-write window, violating the HUMAN-only acceptance boundary.
findings.recommended_action: Require a proven atomic compare-and-set that binds both the ledger source version and authoritative revocation sequence; if none exists, state the acceptance TOCTOU residual explicitly and keep dependency use fail-closed through a fresh authority-sequence check and a defined conflict state.

findings.claim: ADMIN_LEDGER_GENESIS cannot simultaneously honor its fixed allowance of one deterministic invocation and obtain the required independent post-write strict-validator/fixture verification before the administrative ledger is accepted; the design defines no pre-ledger authorization or accounting path for that additional independent activity.
findings.evidence_excerpt: a fixed allowance of one deterministic tool invocation, zero model calls
findings.impact: Genesis either cannot close or must hide/self-verify pre-ledger work; accepting the latter weakens the trust root for all later administrative accounting and P15 admission evidence.
findings.recommended_action: Have the HUMAN genesis decision bind a finite pre-ledger seed envelope with distinct exact writer and independent-verifier invocations, limits, and immutable receipts, while preserving zero mission attempts; seed sequence zero only after those receipts and the HUMAN acceptance record are hash-bound.
